Crypto exchange proxies (COIN, BMAS) are leveraged to Bitcoin adoption and US regulatory clarity, but Indonesia's own crypto-tax regime and rupiah volatility cap upside, favoring selective exposure.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's new feed-in tariffs and local content rules are accelerating domestic solar and biomass project awards, favoring listed players like POWR and 051910 over import-dependent rivals.
US climate-tech names remain hostage to high interest rates and delayed IRA guidance, making them tactical shorts versus resilient Indonesian utility-scale developers.
Waste-to-energy mandates in Jakarta and Surabaya are creating recurring revenue streams for mid-cap operators like HGII and LAPD, insulated from commodity price swings.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables dip is a buying window: POWR's +8.98% and 051910's +8.12% signal domestic policy tailwinds, while US names like PLUG lag. Rotate into local solar/waste-to-energy plays with government PPAs, avoid US hydrogen until rates ease. Add on weakness, target 15% upside in 90 days.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rising middle-class disposable income in tier-2/3 cities continues to drive volume growth for affordable packaged foods and beverages, favoring low-priced, high-turnover FMCG names.
Digital distribution and direct-to-consumer channels are structurally lowering go-to-market costs for small-cap consumer brands, enabling faster share gains against incumbents.
Import substitution in packaging and raw materials, supported by government local-content rules, is improving gross margins for domestic producers like YUPI and BTEK.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in small-cap consumer names with confirmed volume (AGAR, YUPI, BTEK) as the sector's relative strength vs. IDX persists; rotate out of laggards into leaders with earnings catalysts. Expect mean-reversion in NAYZ/DAYA after outsized moves—trim into strength. Maintain overweight on staples for defensive positioning ahead of rupiah volatility.

Rotate into laggards with strong cash flows, as sector breadth remains healthy and foreign flows supportive.

Rotate into PORT for toll-road-linked distribution exposure, and hold AMKBY for US e-commerce spillover. Avoid chasing HATM's single-day spike without volume confirmation; keep logistics beta at neutral with selective names only.
